scope: Original frozen candidate run only; later amendments or retests are not included.
method: Independent model grading of each actual scenario response against the frozen input and predeclared material criteria; actor self-scores were not used. Exact excerpts below support the judgments; each full response was reviewed.

integrity.provenanceLimit: Output provenance fields are actor-reported; no full tool-log audit or enforced-isolation claim is made.
integrity.reportedReadAllowlistAudit: The coordinator reports all actor-declared read paths within the allowlist; this is a self-reported exposure audit, not tool-trace or enforced-isolation proof.

crossCuttingAudit.nonFailingIdObservation: collaborative-feature-definition B proposes an E3 draft while preserving E2/P7 history. This is recorded as a draft revision observation, not a demonstrated overwrite of a stable shared ID.
crossCuttingAudit.unsupportedRatingObservations: feature-risk-analysis assigns HIGH impact in both cases without supplied impact-rating context. B additionally assigns MEDIUM likelihood, which violates its explicit unknown-probability criterion.
crossCuttingAudit.separateFormatObservation: Four scenario B responses exceed the coordinator-reported 220-word protocol limit under whitespace counting: clean-delivery-workflow 223, feature-decomposition 231, feature-risk-analysis 224, and java-testing-strategy 225. These protocol deviations are separate from material domain results.

evaluatorLimitations: The judge is a model, not an independent human or executable oracle; qualitative judgments may be mistaken.
The grader was separate from the response actors but previously expanded the scenario and criterion wording. These are known development cases, not held-out evaluation.
This was an output-only exercise. Advice and status reasoning were assessed; no repository repair, deployment, or scenario test execution was demonstrated.
A and B for each skill shared one fresh actor session, so within-pair contrast awareness may affect responses.
Only the candidate condition was evaluated. There is no original-skill or no-skill baseline and no measured improvement or causal skill-attribution claim.
There was one response per scenario, with inherited model settings and no repeated-run stability estimate.
Skill loading was explicit; automatic skill selection and out-of-scope trigger behavior were not evaluated.

The harness used procedural read allowlists and a shared filesystem, not enforced sandbox isolation. Missing neighboring skill resources mentioned in responses are harness limitations, not automatically scenario failures.
